subject: Sparka Labs — dedicated fleet footprint workshop and traffic sketch
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver@sparka.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Sparka Labs — dedicated fleet footprint workshop and traffic sketch

Oliver — thanks for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, we want to draft a short traffic and token profile so we can size a recommended Dedicated footprint and identify sensible fallback & canary policies. Could you reply with the items below (a quick table is perfect) so we can run initial throughput sims?

Quick ask (highest value first):
- Typical and peak concurrent sessions (by daypart if you have it).
- Average prompt tokens and average response tokens (percentiles: median, p90, p99 if available).
- Percent of requests that stream vs non-stream.
- Long-tail / outlier responses (examples) and expected frequency (e.g., 1% of calls > 2k tokens).
- Typical user session duration and whether KV cache is reused across requests.
- Desired latency SLO (p95/p99) and if you prefer throughput over latency in bursts.
- Any scheduled marketing events or known peak windows in the next 90 days.

If you can drop current telemetry (CSV) or a short export of sample requests, that helps us move fast. We can then sketch GPU SKU mixes and a pilot plan (60-day pilot recommended for production parity).

I'll draft an initial set of sizing assumptions and share a workbook for you to sanity-check once I have the numbers.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

From: Oliver James <oliver@sparka.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya R. <maya@prospects.sparka.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparka Labs — dedicated fleet footprint workshop and traffic sketch

Hi Stephanie — appreciated the convo. Attached are two exports (sparka_api_telemetry_q1.csv and user_sessions_summary_q1.pdf) that cover the telemetry we have for Q1. High-level numbers below (we cleaned/hash PII in the CSV):

- Typical concurrent sessions (weekday daytime): ~800 (SD ~150).
- Evening steady state: ~1,200.
- Peak marketing-driven bursts (we ran one promo in March): short 2–4 hour peaks up to ~6,500 concurrent sessions.

Token profile (sampled from 500k requests):
- Prompt tokens: median 43, p90 120, p99 380.
- Response tokens: median 280, p90 760, p99 2,100. Average response ~320 tokens.
- Long-tail: ~0.6% of requests > 3k response tokens (mostly batch reports / export jobs).

Behavioral notes:
- ~70% of calls are non-streaming (single response returned), ~30% use streaming for interactive chat.
- Sessions typically last 6–12 minutes; many users have multi-turn interactions (avg 4 turns).
- KV caching: we reuse cached prefixes for ~55% of repeated requests during a session, but cache hit quality varies.

SLO: We currently aim for p95 < 500ms for interactive flows and accept higher latency for batch-like exports. But if possible we'd like p95 closer to 300–400ms for interactive chat in production.

Timeline/procurement: We're hoping to run a pilot in June and decide on committed capacity by late Q3. Maya on our side is coordinating procurement.

Thanks — attaching CSV & PDF now.

—Oliver
Head of Platform
Sparka Labs
oliver@sparka.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver@sparka.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparka Labs — dedicated fleet footprint workshop and traffic sketch

Thanks for the telemetry, Oliver — this is very helpful. Quick internal notes and a few follow-ups so our sizing assumptions match reality: (I've pasted Oliver's key lines below for context)

> - Peak marketing-driven bursts ... up to ~6,500 concurrent sessions.
> - Response tokens: median 280, p90 760, p99 2,100.
> - ~70% non-streaming, ~30% streaming.

Ben's follow-ups (short):
1) For the ~0.6% long-tail export jobs: are those triggered via an internal scheduled job or on-demand by users? If scheduled, what's the cadence (daily, hourly)?
2) Can you share an anonymized sample of token-length histograms per endpoint? That helps our continuous-batching model. The CSV you sent is great but a per-endpoint slice speeds up our kernel-selection sims.
3) For KV cache reuse: is the cache keyed at session-level or tenant-level? You mentioned 55% cache reuse — is that mostly within a session or across sessions for the same user?
4) Streaming behavior: when streaming, do you call OpenAI-style chunked increments, or is it server-sent-events? Any throttling on chunk size we should know about?

We'll drop a sizing assumptions workbook (redwood_sizing_assumptions.xlsx) with our default occupancy and oversubscription guardrails. That will include a few SKU mixes (A100-style vs H100-style equivalents) and a recommended conservative pilot-sized fleet for the June pilot.

If convenient, can we set a 30–45 minute technical workshop early next week to walk the telemetry and run a quick traffic-slicer exercise? I can share a screen and we can prototype a burst routing policy.

Cheers —
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Oliver James <oliver@sparka.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya R. <maya@prospects.sparka.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparka Labs — dedicated fleet footprint workshop and traffic sketch

Ben / Stephanie — apologies for the quick reply window, weekend here but wanted to confirm:

1) The long-tail exports are 75% on-demand (user initiated) and 25% scheduled nightly reports (run between 02:00–03:00 PDT). We'll flag those as "low SLO" in the CSV by endpoint.
2) We'll extract per-endpoint histograms for the two top endpoints ("/chat/compose" and "/reports/generate") and upload to the Drive link you shared by Monday.
3) KV cache is session-level for interactive chat; tenant-level caching happens only for a small set of ML-backed lookups (~8% of traffic). Most cache reuse you saw is within session.
4) Streaming is chunked server-sent-events (SSE) with 100–300 token chunks typically. No client-side throttling configured today.

We're good for a short workshop — Monday 10:00am PT works for us. Procurement note: we'll aim to finalize pilot budget this week so we can move forward with a June start.

Thanks —
Oliver
